title: Chicken Noodle Soup
subtitle: A restorative classic
excerpt: A deeply comforting bowl built on a clear, herb-scented broth with tender shredded chicken and soft egg noodles. It is the kind of soup that improves with a night in the fridge, making it an excellent cook-ahead meal for the week.
sourceNotes: Chicken noodle soup has roots across many cultures, but the American version became iconic through Jewish immigrant cooking and was further popularised by tinned soups from the early twentieth century. This version draws on the tradition of simmering a whole bird or bone-in pieces for maximum flavour.

recipe.batchNotes: Doubles easily in a large stockpot. Freeze the broth and chicken separately without noodles, then cook fresh noodles when reheating.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make the broth and shred the chicken the day before. Add noodles only when reheating so they do not go mushy.

content.text: Starting the chicken in cold stock and bringing it up slowly draws more flavour into the broth than dropping it into boiling liquid. Pull the chicken out just as it is cooked through so it stays juicy when you shred it back in at the end.
Put the chicken thighs, onion quarters, parsley stalks, bay leaves, thyme, and garlic into the stockpot. Pour over the stock and set over a medium heat.
Bring slowly to a gentle simmer, skimming off any foam that rises to the surface. Do not let it boil hard.
After 20 minutes, add the carrot and celery. Continue simmering for a further 15 minutes until the vegetables are tender and the chicken is cooked through.
Lift out the chicken thighs and shred the meat with two forks. Discard the onion quarters, bay leaves, thyme stalks, garlic, and parsley stalks.
Add the egg noodles to the simmering broth and cook according to pack instructions, usually 4 to 6 minutes.
Return the shredded chicken to the pot. Taste and season with salt and pepper. Ladle into bowls and scatter over the parsley leaves.

items.cause: The soup boiled too hard rather than simmering gently.
items.fix: Simmer low and skim foam early for a clearer broth.

items.cause: They sat in the hot broth too long after cooking.
items.fix: Cook noodles just before serving; do not leave them in the soup.

items.cause: It was overcooked or cooked at too high a temperature.
items.fix: Pull chicken out as soon as it is cooked through, then shred.
